ev.t:
# Invite users and assign seats
Each person who signs in to InvoicePilot uses one seat. You can invite as many users as you have seats.
1. Go to Settings > Users.
2. Click Invite User and enter their email.
3. Pick a role: Admin, Accountant, Staff, or Read-only.
4. Click Send Invite. The invite link expires after 7 days.
If you run out of seats, an account owner can buy more from Settings > Subscription > Add Seats.

# Users endpoint
Added to API v2 on 2026-07-01. See the API changelog.
| Method | Path | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | /v2/users | List users and their roles |
| POST | /v2/users/invite | Invite a user. The invite link expires after 7 days |
| PATCH | /v2/users/{user_id} | Change a user's role |
| DELETE | /v2/users/{user_id} | Remove a user and free the seat |
Assigning a custom role through the API needs Enterprise. On other plans, use Admin, Accountant, Staff, or Read-only.

# Enterprise onboarding checklist
1. Kickoff with the named CSM
2. Set up custom roles and invite users (invite links expire after 7 days)
3. Connect bank feeds (unlimited on Enterprise)
4. Set up webhooks (up to 25 endpoints)
5. Review the audit log settings (13 months of history)

# Renewals and license expiry
Every license runs for 12 months from its order date. You can see each license's expiry date under Settings > Subscription.
Licenses renew for another 12 months when you place a Renewal order. We email the account owner 60, 30, and 7 days before expiry.
If a license expires, users on those seats lose sign-in access. Data is kept for 90 days.

# Seats and adding seats
InvoicePilot is billed per seat per year. One seat lets one user sign in.
## Adding seats
Account owners can add seats from Settings > Subscription > Add Seats. Added seats are billed at the plan's full per-seat price and start their own 12-month term from the day you add them. They are not prorated.

q: A customer sent an invoice by mistake. Can they just delete it?
exp: No. Sent invoices can't be deleted; they must be voided, which keeps them in records with a VOID watermark. Only drafts can be deleted.
gev: Draft invoices can be deleted. Sent invoices cannot be deleted; void them instead so your records stay complete.

ev.t:
# Void or delete an invoice
Draft invoices can be deleted. Sent invoices cannot be deleted; void them instead so your records stay complete.
1. Open the invoice.
2. Click More > Void.
3. Enter a reason. The reason is kept with the invoice.
Voided invoices stay in reports with a zero balance and show a VOID watermark.

# Pause or stop a recurring invoice
Open the recurring profile and click Pause. No invoices are generated while it is paused.
When you resume, the next invoice goes out on the next scheduled date. Missed dates are not sent.
To stop for good, click Stop. Invoices already sent are not affected.

# Troubleshooting: reminders sent for voided invoices
Invoices voided with a bulk action kept their scheduled payment reminders, so clients got reminders for void invoices.
This is BUG-2200-03 (Medium). It affected 2.2.0. It was fixed in 2.2.1.

# Note: long invoice workaround for support
For BUG-2310-02, tell customers to send the invoice link. Do not suggest splitting invoices unless the customer asks; it changes their numbering.

# Gap in invoice numbers
Customer: We deleted a draft and now INV-000213 is missing from the sequence. Our auditor asked about it.
Support agent: That's BUG-2000-04: on 2.0.0, deleting a draft uses up its number. It's fixed in 2.0.1. The gap stays, but the Invoice Register report shows the deleted draft for your auditor.
Customer: Got it, thanks.

q: An integration got error IP-4220. What does it mean, and should it retry?
exp: IP-4220 (HTTP 422) means validation failed; the message says which field. It should not be retried.
gev: | 422 | IP-4220 | Validation failed; see message | No |
ans: Error IP-4220 means validation failed; see the message [support/report-a-bug#0]. It should not be retried [support/report-a-bug#0].

ev.t:
# 422 IP-4220 validation error
Customer: Our integration gets IP-4220 on some invoices. Message says line_items[2].quantity must be greater than 0. Should we retry?
Support agent: IP-4220 means validation failed, and the message tells you which field. It is not retryable: fix the data (here, a quantity of 0) and send it again. If you want more detail, newer responses may include a subcode like IP-4221 for line item problems.
Customer: That's not great, but we'll use the workaround.

# Error subcodes
| HTTP | Code | Meaning | Retry? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 404 | IP-4041 | The resource exists but belongs to another organization | No |
| 409 | IP-4091 | A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processed | Yes, after 1 second |
| 422 | IP-4221 | Line item validation failed (quantity, rate, or tax) | No |
| 422 | IP-4222 | The currency is not enabled for this organization | No |
| 422 | IP-4223 | The customer is archived | No |
| 422 | IP-4224 | The invoice is void and cannot be changed | No |
| 422 | IP-4225 | The estimate is not accepted, so it cannot be converted | No |
| 422 | IP-4226 | Webhook URL must use HTTPS | No |
| 429 | IP-4291 | Too many concurrent requests (more than 10 in flight per key) | Yes, after Retry-After |
| 503 | IP-5031 | Payment processor unavailable | Yes, with backoff |

# Error codes
| HTTP | Code | Meaning | Retry? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | IP-4000 | Malformed request or invalid JSON | No |
| 401 | IP-4010 | Missing or invalid API key | No |
| 403 | IP-4030 | Key lacks permission, or the limit for your plan is reached | No |
| 404 | IP-4040 | Resource not found | No |
| 409 | IP-4090 | Idempotency-Key was reused with a different request body | No |
| 422 | IP-4220 | Validation failed; see message | No |
| 429 | IP-4290 | Rate limit exceeded; wait for Retry-After | Yes |
| 500 | IP-5000 | Internal error | Yes, with backoff |
| 503 | IP-5030 | Bank feed provider unavailable | Yes, with backoff |

# Does the Python SDK retry on its own?
Yes. client = Client(max_retries=3) and it retries 429, 500 and 503. It won't retry IP-4220 validation errors.

# How to report a bug
Open a ticket with the steps to reproduce, the version shown under Help > About, and any error code such as IP-4220.
If the bug is already tracked, support links your ticket to its BUG- ID and you get an email when it is fixed.

# 429 IP-4290 during nightly import
Customer: We keep hitting IP-4290. Can you raise our rate limit?
Support agent: IP-4290 means the per-minute rate limit was reached. Your plan allows 60 requests per minute. Wait for the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then retry. If you run many requests in parallel, also watch for IP-4291, which is the separate limit of 10 requests in flight.
Customer: OK. Please let us know when it's fixed.

## Root cause
The aggregator had an outage. Our sync retried too fast and was throttled after they recovered.
## Resolution
Added jittered backoff to sync retries. IP-5030 is the correct code for this case and clients should retry with backoff.

### "We heard about bugs in 2.3.1."
Be honest: BUG-2310-01 and BUG-2310-02 are open with workarounds. Don't promise a fix date.
### "Starter is too limited."
Starter has every feature; plans differ by limits. Show the plan comparison.

# SSO when?
We need SAML. Sales said 'soon'. Nothing on the roadmap page.
Reply: same. No date anywhere.

q: A Professional customer hit their per-minute API limit. What is that limit, and which error code did they get?
exp: 300 requests per minute on Professional; going over returns HTTP 429 with IP-4290 and a Retry-After header.
gev: | Professional | 300 |
| 429 | IP-4290 | Rate limit exceeded; wait for Retry-After | Yes |
ans: The per-minute limit for a Professional customer is 300 requests [engineering/runbook-rate-limit-requests#0].

ev.t:
# Concurrency limits
Besides the per-minute rate limit, each API key can have at most 10 requests in flight at once.
An 11th parallel request gets HTTP 429 with IP-4291 and a Retry-After header. This is different from IP-4290, which means the per-minute limit was reached.
The concurrency limit is the same on every plan. Per-minute limits are 60, 300, or 1,000 by plan.

# IP-4291 errors after scaling workers
Customer: We moved our sync to 16 parallel workers and now get IP-4291. We're well under our per-minute limit.
Support agent: IP-4291 is the concurrency limit: at most 10 requests in flight per API key, on every plan. IP-4290 is the per-minute limit. Keep 10 or fewer requests in parallel and retry after Retry-After.

# ADR-017: Per-key concurrency limit
## Decision
Limit each API key to 10 requests in flight, on every plan. Over the limit returns 429 IP-4291.
## Why
A few integrations ran 50+ parallel workers and caused slowdowns for everyone, while staying under their per-minute limit.

# Runbook: rate limit increase requests
Per-minute limits are 60 (Starter), 300 (Professional), 1,000 (Enterprise). Only Enterprise can get a custom limit, approved by the CSM and platform team. The concurrency limit of 10 is never raised.

## Headers
Every v2 response includes:
- X-RateLimit-Limit: your limit per minute
- X-RateLimit-Remaining: requests left in this window
- X-RateLimit-Reset: Unix time when the window resets
When you go over, you get HTTP 429 with error code IP-4290 and a Retry-After header in seconds.
Note: in 2.2.0 these headers were missing (BUG-2200-02). Fixed in 2.3.0.

ev.t:
# Create your organization
Your organization holds your company profile, base currency, fiscal year, and users.
1. Sign up at app.invoicepilot.example and verify your email.
2. Enter your company name, country, and industry.
3. Choose your base currency. This cannot be changed after your first transaction.
4. Set your fiscal year start month.
5. Choose a plan: Starter, Professional, or Enterprise.

# Exchange rates
InvoicePilot updates exchange rates once a day from a market data provider. You can also enter a rate by hand on any invoice.
Reports convert foreign amounts to your base currency using the rate saved on each transaction.

# Troubleshooting: recurring preview shows the wrong currency
The preview of upcoming recurring invoices showed the base currency symbol for clients billed in another currency. The invoices themselves were correct.
This is BUG-2110-01 (Low). It affected 2.1.1. It was fixed in 2.2.0.

# InvoicePilot Release Notes v2.0.0 "Nova"
A redesigned core app with native multi-currency support.
## New Features
- Multi-currency invoicing: bill customers in their local currency with daily exchange-rate updates.
- New dashboard with at-a-glance revenue, outstanding invoices, and expense trends.
- Redesigned navigation and settings area for faster access to organization preferences.

# Enable multi-currency
Multi-currency invoicing arrived in 2.0.0. It lets you bill customers in their own currency.
1. Go to Settings > Currencies.
2. Turn on Multi-currency.
3. Add the currencies you need.
4. Set each customer's currency on their profile.
> Note: Existing single-currency organizations are not affected until multi-currency is turned on.

# Enable multi-currency
Multi-currency invoicing arrived in 2.0.0. It lets you bill customers in their own currency.
1. Go to Settings > Currencies.

ev.t:
# How recurring invoice schedules handle time zones
Starting in 2.3.1, recurring invoice schedules are calculated in UTC internally. Send times are still shown in your organization's local time zone.
This change fixed BUG-2100-02, where schedules calculated in local time skipped a cycle when daylight-saving time shifted.
No action is needed. Existing schedules were migrated automatically when 2.3.1 rolled out.

## Upgrade Notes
Recurring invoice schedules created in 2.1.0 are calculated in your organization's local timezone; see Known Issues below for a daylight-saving edge case.

# Troubleshooting: a recurring invoice skipped a cycle
Cause: BUG-2100-02, "Recurring invoices skip a cycle across DST changes". Recurring invoice schedules calculated in local time skipped a billing cycle when daylight-saving time shifted, causing missed invoices for some customers.
Affected versions: 2.1.0 through 2.3.0. Fixed in 2.3.1.

# Recurring profiles endpoint
next_run_at is returned in UTC. Since 2.3.1 schedules are calculated in UTC.

# Recurring invoices: frequently asked questions
### Which time zone do schedules use?
Since 2.3.1, UTC internally. Dates are shown in your local time.

mut: Temporal flip: says UTC was already used on 2.3.0
